record.tranche_reason: The post reports measurements of activation-space amplification maxima and discusses their interpretation, but does not test whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs.
record.gate_note: The reported maxima are directions in activation space, not individual neurons or a measure of neuron polysemanticity. Activation-steered continuations are induced outputs and are not evidence about naturally occurring polysemanticity. The post also mentions results from prior work, which are not recorded as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The post never measures individual neurons or how many of them are polysemantic. It finds a few maxima of a channel-amplification score in activation space for GPT-2 and Llama. It mentions superposition only as background, citing Computation in Superposition, and gives no result on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct. The author argues that amplification maxima are few and model-natural. He guesses they are mostly not conventional features, the possible exception being the abstract-noun direction. He suggests they are computational processes with mixed statistical signatures. He draws no conclusion about neuron polysemanticity.
record.recipe_differences: The study optimizes and measures channel amplification in activation space; it does not use the original neuron-inspection approach to test polysemanticity.
record.method_sensitivity: The set of maxima is reported to depend on training protocol, whitening, data distribution, and threshold choice. The post also says unwhitened scoring finds fewer maxima; bigram data replaces one maximum and adds two others.

fits_no_version.finding: In gpt2-small layer 6 (whitened, simple gradient ascent), a channel-amplification objective converges to exactly 4 activation-space maxima. The atlas largely persists under bigram-only data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLP layers of trained language models have very few strongly amplified (denoised) activation directions. These are largely determined by the weights.

fits_no_version.finding: 3–6 reachable maxima are reported across GPT-2 layers and Llama. A commenter reports that about half of attractor descriptions (332/628) classified new snippets correctly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Amplification-attractor directions recur across models and layers. They are only partly describable by simple semantic labels.

record.problems: The author describes the work as preliminary. The main detailed taxonomy is for gpt2-small layer 6, and the post says the atlas depends on choices such as whitening, threshold, training protocol, and data distribution. Some generated examples are described as cherry-picked. The cross-model/layer summary gives a range without per-model or per-layer values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results on individual-neuron polysemanticity are reported. Activation-steered continuations and other interpretive examples are omitted because they do not measure naturally occurring polysemanticity.

untested.parts: No share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens, and no layer-wise neuron counts.
No test of whether superposition causes neuron polysemanticity. Superposition appears only as theoretical background.
No test of polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
No polysemantic-neuron share by architecture or regularization. Llama (SwiGLU) is compared only in terms of amplification maxima.
Canonical polysemantic neurons are not re-examined.
Measurement dependence is shown only for amplification maxima (threshold, whitening), not for classifying neurons as polysemantic.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the post does not discuss polysemantic neurons; it only cites superposition work as background. The comment thread also reports that random-init models give zero attractors, which is not in the rows. It is not relevant to any version.

versions.untested_parts: Individual image-classifier neurons and their responses to unrelated image inputs.
The share of transformer MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, and differences across layers.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by superposition or feature-capacity pressure.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure from initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Polysemantic-neuron share, its change with architecture or training, and any performance cost of lowering it.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons detect a shared feature or related jobs when examined with better tools.
Whether classifying neurons as polysemantic depends on activation range or explanation-scoring choices.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Gradient-ascent flows on the channel amplification score from text activations to local maxima.

conditions.value: whitened metric; simple gradient ascent trained to completion

rows.measure: Number and structure of reachable local maxima of the channel amplification score
rows.value: Exactly 4 local maxima; 3 are ±coplanar with the origin. The author reports that over a hundred thousand tokens converge to these same four points.
rows.note: This is a count of amplification-score maxima, not a count or classification of neurons.
rows.check: Linking is correct: this counts score maxima, not neurons. Note that this count holds only for the whitened, simple-ascent setup. The author reports fewer maxima without whitening.

rows.subject: GPT-2 and Llama (aggregate, as reported)
rows.operation_detail: Compared reachable amplification maxima across architectures and layers.

conditions.value: GPT-2 layers and Llama; exact per-model and per-layer values not stated

rows.value: Between 3 and 6 reachable maxima; described as robust across architectures and layers. Llama is described as having a small number of minima and comparable types of structure.
rows.note: The post gives no per-model or per-layer counts here; this result concerns maxima, not polysemantic neurons.
rows.check: The post gives only an aggregate range of 3–6 maxima, with no per-model or per-layer values. It concerns activation-space maxima, not neurons.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Recomputed the amplification-maximizer atlas using a bigram language distribution instead of the usual text distribution.
rows.measure: Identity and persistence of amplification and attenuation maxima
rows.baseline: Usual data distribution: the four-feature setup described earlier
rows.value: Almost the same features were found; the abstract-nouns/Names-of-God feature was replaced by a mid-word-fragments feature, other amplifying and attenuating features were preserved, and two new features appeared: listing spaces and an extra spaces feature.
rows.note: The comparison is about the atlas of activation-space directions, not a measurement of neuron polysemanticity.
rows.check: Linking is correct. This compares the atlas of directions under bigram versus normal data, not neuron polysemanticity.
